content.comment_body: Hello, I have a driver with a 0-10V input. When [product_name] sends 0 Vdc or 3.2Vdc, the voltage increases to 4.2Vdc once connected. How can this be resolved? The driver requires a minimum current input of 0.15 mA. This driver accepts a dimming signal of 0-10V, variable resistance from 0-100kOhms, or a PWM signal with 0-100% duty cycle.

The issue is with the input interface because it is not a standard type. [product_name] can only control typical 0-10V interfaces reliably. This topic has been discussed often in the German section of the forum. Potential solutions include: using a resistor in parallel with the analog output, where you need to determine the correct resistance value; or using an isolating amplifier for 0-10V conversion, which I consider the best choice.

I experienced a similar issue when connecting to an LED driver and was able to fix it by placing a 10k resistor in parallel across the output. More details can be found at: [url]. That said, [user_name]'s suggestion to use an isolating amplifier is the most effective method, though it is more costly. My setup has been working for over 8 months without any problems.

analysis.insight_summary: Users run into compatibility challenges when connecting [product_name] to drivers expecting a 0-10V signal, as the output voltage can behave inconsistently due to the driver's minimum current requirement. Addressing this requires additional components or adjustments, disrupting expectations of straightforward device integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to work seamlessly with any 0-10V dimming driver and provide stable, accurate voltage outputs without needing extra setup or components.
